div.head: Af El. 23
div.ab: Gif oxa oðres monnes oxan gewundige, ⁊ he ðonne dead sie, bebycggen þone oxan ⁊ hæbben him þæt weorð gemǽne ⁊ eac ðæt flǽsc swa ðæs deadan. Gif se hlaford þonne wisse, þæt se oxa hnitol wære, ⁊ hine healdan nolde, selle him oðerne oxan fore ⁊ hæbbe him eall ðæt flǽsc.

Gif óxa oðres mannes oxan gewundige, ⁊ he ðonne dead sy, bebicgan ðone óxan ⁊ habbon hím þæt weorð gemæne ⁊ eac þæt flæsc swa ðæs deadan. Gif se hlaford þonne wiste, þæt se oxa hnitol wære, ⁊ he hyne healdan nolde, sylle him oðerne oxan fore ⁊ hæbbe him eall þæt flæsc.

Gif oxa oþres mannes oxan gewundie, ⁊ he þonne dead sy, bebicgan þone oxan ⁊ habben heom þæt weorþ gemæne ⁊ eac þæt flæsc swa ðæs deadan. Gif se hlaford ðonne wiste, þæt se oxa hnitol wære, ⁊ hine healdan nolde, sylle him oþerne oxan fore ⁊ hæbbe him eal þæt flæsc.

Si bos alienus bouem alterius uulnerauerit, et ille mortuus fuerit, uendent bouem uiuum et diuident pretium; cadauer autem mortuum inter se dispertient. Si autem sciébat, quod bos cornupeta esset ab heri et nudiustertius, et non custodiuit eum dominus suus, reddet bouem pro boue et cadauer integrum accipiet.

Gif oxa oðres monnes oxan gewundige, ⁊ he ðonne dead sie, bebycggen þone oxan ⁊ hæbben him þæt weorð gemæne ⁊ eac ðæt flǽsc swa ðæs deadan. Gif se hlaford þonne wisse, þæt se oxa hnitol wære, ⁊ hine healdan nolde, selle him oðerne oxan fore ⁊ hæbbe him eall ðæt flæsc.

Wenn ein Ochs den Ochsen eines anderen Mannes verwundet, und der [verwundete] dann todt ist, mögen beide Herren jenen [stössigen] verkaufen und sich den Preis gemeinschaftlich behalten und ebenso das Fleisch des todten. Wenn aber der [erste] Herr wusste, dass der Ochs stössig wäre, und ihn nicht [in Hut] halten wollte, gebe er ihm [dem zweiten] einen anderen Ochsen statt dessen und behalte sich das ganze Fleisch [des gestossenen].

If an ox wounds another man’s ox, and the [wounded one] then is dead, let both owners sell that [goring] one and keep the price between them in common, and likewise the flesh of the dead one. But if the [first] owner knew that the ox was given to goring, and would not keep it [under guard], let him give him [the second owner] another ox in its place and keep for himself all the flesh [of the gored one].

If an ox wounds another’s ox, and the latter then dies, let them sell the [living] ox and share the payment and also the flesh of the dead one. If, however, the lord knew that the ox was given to pushing with its horns and he would not restrain it, let him give the ox [to the owner of the dead ox] and let him have all the flesh [as well].
